Investors vote to approve the $110 billion buyout by Paramount Skydance amid ongoing changes for the entertainment industry and noisy resistance from Hollywood's creative community Warner Bros. Discovery shareholders voted Thursday to approve the company's sale to Paramount Skydance for $110 billion. The era of Hollywood's "Big Five" studios is one step closer to its end. Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) shareholders voted Thursday to approve the sale of the company to Paramount Skydance (PSKY) for $110 billion, reducing the number of major independent studios in Hollywood by one amid broad changes for the entertainment industry. The deal has been met with vociferous resistance from Hollywood's unions and creative community, with Democratic attorneys general from several states promising to heavily scrutinize the sale.

Earlier this year, the streaming and entertainment industry witnessed one of its most high-stakes megadeals ever, stunning industry observers. Not only is it historic in its size, but it is also predicted to disrupt Hollywood and the media business as we know it. After years of Warner Bros. Discovery struggling under the weight of billions of dollars in debt, compounded by declining cable viewership and fierce competition from streaming platforms, the company has been considering major strategic changes, including selling its entertainment assets to one of its rivals. ---

Attorneys General around the country, as well as many politicians, have discussed mounting a legal challenge to Paramount Skydance’s mega purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery. Thus far none of them have done anything to actually stop it. But some normal, unelected people have. Five Paramount+ subscribers have filed a federal antitrust lawsuit in California to halt the sale. Yes, the people are suing to stop this Warner Bros...

After years of Warner Bros. [Lähde: Morningstar | URL: https://www.morningstar.com/news/marketwatch/20260423295/as-warner-bros-shareholders-ok-sale-to-paramount-a-legendary-studio-approaches-the-end-of-an-era]
Investors vote to approve the $110 billion buyout by Paramount Skydance amid ongoing changes for the entertainment industry and noisy resistance from Hollywood's creative community

Warner Bros. Discovery shareholders voted Thursday to approve the company's sale to Paramount Skydance for $110 billion.

The era of Hollywood's "Big Five" studios is one step closer to its end.

Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) shareholders voted Thursday to approve the sale of the company to Paramount Skydance (PSKY) for $110 billion, reducing the number of major independent studios in Hollywood by one amid broad changes for the entertainment industry.

The deal has been met with vociferous resistance from Hollywood's unions and creative community, with Democratic attorneys general from several states promising to heavily scrutinize the sale.

But the Warner Bros. board had unanimously approved the transaction and multiple proxy advisory firms had recommended shareholders back it, so the approval by investors was not a surprise. A year ago, Warner Bros. shares were trading at around $8, so the $31-per-share offer from Paramount was a strong enticement.

Shares of Paramount fell 4.5% on Thursday, while Warner Bros. shares dipped 1.6%.

The transaction will help usher in a new period in Hollywood, which has been faced with broad changes in recent years as consumer habits have shifted rapidly from going to movie theaters and watching cable television to an era of streaming and short-form online content.

Many in Hollywood fear that the consolidation of Warner Bros. and Paramount will result in wide-scale layoffs and fewer jobs across the industry.

Paramount CEO David Ellison has said he plans to operate the two film and television studios independently, with the aim of producing up to 30 films a year between them, up from the 20 they collectively put out last year. But many industry watchers have questioned whether that level of output is possible.

The last remaining steps for the deal lie with regulators, but Ellison and his father, Oracle (ORCL) co-founder Larry Ellison, enjoy good relations with the Trump administration, which has signaled that it doesn't intend to stand in the way of the transaction.

Paramount has said it expects the deal to close during the third quarter of this year.

In February, Paramount was able to wrest Warner Bros. away from rival Netflix (NFLX), which had earlier reached a deal to acquire Warner Bros.' studio and streaming divisions for $82.7 billion

---

[Lähde: The American Prospect | URL: https://prospect.org/2026/04/27/warner-bros-sale-ellisons-shareholder-capitalism-merger-paramount/]
When Warner Bros. Discovery shareholders voted last Thursday on the Ellison family’s purchase of the company, the result wasn’t exactly close. Approximately 1.743 billion shares were cast in favor of the sale, while just 16.3 million were cast against it. That’s a ratio of roughly 99-to-1.

I can’t say with complete certainty that had the vote been taken among Warner Bros. employees and the Hollywood community at large, the ratio would also have been 99-to-1, but in this case against, not for. But by all available, if imperfect, metrics, including the signatures of more than 4,000 media industry workers on a letter predicting industry disaster if the sale went through, it’s clear that the people most affected by the sale were resolutely against it. Not a single actor, director, screenwriter, producer, cinematographer, editor, composer, musician, stunt worker, grip—anyone who actually works in the industry—has come out in favor of the deal. Not one. Maybe their vote wouldn’t have been 99-to-1 against. More likely, it would have been 100-to-0.

The industry workers have good reason to be opposed. As I noted one week ago, deals of this kind saddle the purchased companies with the debt the buyer incurred to make the deal—in this case, it’s a cool $79 billion—that compel cutbacks in production in order to pay off some of that debt. That was exactly what happened when Disney bought 21st Century Fox in 2019, despite the assurances that Fox would remain unscathed. Instead, Fox barely exists today, and the signatories to that letter warned of similar consequences coming to Warners, which has produced many more and generally better pictures in recent years than the Ellison-owned Paramount. Indeed, Warners films took in $4 billion in revenue last year (an all-time record) while also winning 11 Oscars (also a record) last month, chiefly for the two most acclaimed studio films of 2025, One Battle After Another and Sinners.

payload.title: Warner Bros. Discoveryn omistajat hyväksyivät 110 miljardin dollarin myynnin Paramountille
payload.summary: Warner Bros. Discoveryn osakkeenomistajat ovat hyväksyneet yhtiön myynnin Paramount Skydancelle. Hollywoodin rakenteita muuttavaa kauppaa vastustetaan kuitenkin sekä alan sisällä että oikeudessa.
payload.content:
Warner Bros. Discoveryn osakkeenomistajat ovat hyväksyneet yhtiön myynnin Paramount Skydancelle noin 110 miljardilla dollarilla. Historiallisen suuri järjestely veisi Hollywoodia kohti tilannetta, jossa yksi merkittävä itsenäinen studio katoaa, mutta kaupan etenemistä varjostavat luovan yhteisön vastustus, viranomaisten lupaama tarkastelu ja Kaliforniassa nostettu kilpailuoikeudellinen kanne.

## Hyväksyntä vie kauppaa eteenpäin

Osakkeenomistajien päätös vie järjestelyä eteenpäin, mutta kauppa on edelleen suunnitteilla. Toteutuessaan se vähentäisi Hollywoodin suurten itsenäisten studioiden määrää yhdellä. Samalla niin kutsutun viiden suuren studion aikakausi olisi askeleen lähempänä loppuaan.

Hollywoodin ammattiliitot ja luova yhteisö ovat vastustaneet järjestelyä voimakkaasti. Useiden osavaltioiden demokraattiset oikeusministerit ovat puolestaan luvanneet tutkia kaupan tarkasti. Oikeusministerien ja poliitikkojen esiin nostamat mahdolliset oikeustoimet eivät kuitenkaan ole toistaiseksi pysäyttäneet järjestelyä.

Kaupan arvosta on esitetty kaksi lähekkäistä lukua. Osakkeenomistajien hyväksymän myynnin hinnaksi on ilmoitettu 110 miljardia dollaria, kun suunnitellun yritysoston arvoksi on ilmoitettu myös 111 miljardia dollaria. Molemmat luvut tekevät kaupasta yhden viihdealan historian suurimmista järjestelyistä.

## Velka ja suoratoistokilpailu muutosten taustalla

Kauppaa edelsivät Warner Bros. Discoveryn pitkään jatkuneet ongelmat. Yhtiötä ovat rasittaneet miljardien dollarien velat, kaapelitelevision katsojamäärien lasku sekä suoratoistopalvelujen kova kilpailu. Näiden paineiden keskellä yhtiö on harkinnut merkittäviä strategisia muutoksia, mukaan lukien viihdeomaisuuden myymistä kilpailijalle.

Järjestelyn mittakaavan odotetaan muuttavan Hollywoodin ja laajemman media-alan voimasuhteita. Paramount Skydancen omistukseen siirtyminen yhdistäisi kaksi suurta viihdealan toimijaa ja poistaisi Warner Bros. Discoveryn itsenäisten suurstudioiden joukosta.

## Paramount+-tilaajat veivät kiistan oikeuteen

Viisi Paramount+-suoratoistopalvelun tilaajaa on nostanut Kaliforniassa liittovaltion kilpailuoikeudellisen kanteen, jolla he pyrkivät pysäyttämään Warner Bros. Discoveryn myynnin. Ennen tilaajien kannetta oikeusministerit ja poliitikot olivat keskustelleet mahdollisista oikeustoimista, mutta nämä puheet eivät olleet johtaneet kaupan pysäyttämiseen.

Osakkeenomistajien hyväksyntä ratkaisi yhden tärkeän vaiheen, mutta vastustus jatkuu nyt sekä Hollywoodin sisällä että liittovaltion tuomioistuimessa.

Noin 110 miljardin dollarin kauppa vähentäisi Hollywoodin suurten itsenäisten studioiden määrää.
Viisi Paramount+-tilaajaa yrittää pysäyttää kaupan Kaliforniassa nostetulla liittovaltion kilpailuoikeudellisella kanteella.

article.source_text:
Learn more about Paramount's planned acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery — a historic Hollywood megadeal valued at $111 billion — as it continues to develop.

Investors vote to approve the $110 billion buyout by Paramount Skydance amid ongoing changes for the entertainment industry and noisy resistance from Hollywood's creative community Warner Bros. Discovery shareholders voted Thursday to approve the company's sale to Paramount Skydance for $110 billion. The era of Hollywood's "Big Five" studios is one step closer to its end. Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) shareholders voted Thursday to approve the sale of the company to Paramount Skydance (PSKY) for $110 billion, reducing the number of major independent studios in Hollywood by one amid broad changes for the entertainment industry. The deal has been met with vociferous resistance from Hollywood's unions and creative community, with Democratic attorneys general from several states promising to heavily scrutinize the sale.

Earlier this year, the streaming and entertainment industry witnessed one of its most high-stakes megadeals ever, stunning industry observers. Not only is it historic in its size, but it is also predicted to disrupt Hollywood and the media business as we know it. After years of Warner Bros. Discovery struggling under the weight of billions of dollars in debt, compounded by declining cable viewership and fierce competition from streaming platforms, the company has been considering major strategic changes, including selling its entertainment assets to one of its rivals. ---

Attorneys General around the country, as well as many politicians, have discussed mounting a legal challenge to Paramount Skydance’s mega purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery. Thus far none of them have done anything to actually stop it. But some normal, unelected people have.
